tagline: US 64 through the waterfall country, from Rosman to Murphy.
intro: US 64 heads west out of Rosman, over Toxaway Falls and through Sapphire Valley to Cashiers, climbs on to Highlands, then drops down the Cullasaja Gorge to Franklin and runs past Chatuge Lake to Murphy. It is 98 miles through five counties, about two and a half hours.

Transylvania County, where the road begins, is known as the Land of the Waterfalls, and some 200 falls lie around the route. Below Highlands the road passes Dry Falls and follows the Cullasaja River down its gorge, where Cullasaja Falls cascades beside a run of blind curves.

moments.title: Highlands
moments.text: At 4,118 feet, a town founded in 1875 where its founders' lines from Chicago to Savannah and New Orleans to New York crossed, on the theory that a great trading center would follow.

moments.title: Bridal Veil Falls
moments.text: A 45-foot fall about 20 feet from the pavement that the highway once ran behind, until ice on the curve sent traffic around the front.

moments.title: Murphy
moments.text: Where the Hiwassee meets the Valley River, the county gave up on brick after three courthouse fires and built in blue marble quarried less than ten miles away.

practical: The state guidebook notes that tractor-trailers are prohibited on this road and that it is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, Waterfall Byway
